title: Opportunistic partition-aware prefill→decode scheduler with clock headroom hints
creator: Ethan Liu
description: Background: Mixed prefill/decode workloads (chat + system prefill) show elevated 99th latency and token jitter on heterogeneous clusters where H100, L40S, and A10 are co-scheduled with varying MIG partitions and non-uniform clock states. Objective: Implement an opportunistic scheduler and kernel-hint layer that coordinates MIG partition choices, GPU clock headroom sampling (NVML), and kernel selection hints so that prefill jobs are packed/stepped to maximize throughput while keeping decode tail latency within SLOs. Approach: 1) Add a lightweight 'clock headroom' signal via nvml sampling aggregated per node and exposed to the runtime. 2) Introduce partition-aware batch placement: prefer placing long prefill batches onto MIG partitions with spare clock headroom and colocate decode-critical lanes on partitions with tighter SLOs. 3) Kernel-hint metadata: expose a short-lived hint attached to requests (prefill vs decode, expected token budget) so the dispatcher can pick the lower-latency kernel variant for decode segments. 4) Prefill→Decode slit scheduling: interleave small decode slices between big prefill batches instead of draining KV cache fully to reduce stall spikes. Constraints: must be safe for Dedicated/Private deployments, support rollback to current kernel-routing logic, and avoid increased TCO by excessive clock boosting. Deliverables: scheduler code, nvml adapter, benchmark harness (H100/L40S/A10), canary rollout plan, and dashboards for cost/latency tradeoffs.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler samples GPU clock headroom at <=100ms interval and exposes signal to dispatcher (nvml adapter merged)
Kernel-hint API added to request metadata and respected by kernel-selection path (fallback to current selection on mismatch)
End-to-end perf test shows >=15% reduction in 99th token latency for mixed prefill/decode synthetic trace on H100 cluster compared to baseline
No more than 5% increase in average token cost across Canary traffic on L40S when opportunistic clock scaling is enabled
Canary rollout supports instant disable and reversion without draining tokens (feature gate + config flag)
Telemetry: per-route charts showing prefill/decode latency breakdown, MIG-utilization, and clock headroom exposure merged to Console

notes: Rollout: start with canary on non-critical routes in eu-west-1, monitor 95/99 latencies and cost, then expand to us-west-2. If 99th latency increases >5% abort.
Operator considerations: Dedicated customers may have nvml disabled in constrained environments; scheduler must gracefully fall back to static heuristics.
Fallbacks: When nvml sampling fails, revert to current kernel-routing logic and mark node as 'headroom unknown' in telemetry.
Future: If successful, extend to per-tenant quotas and autoscaling hints for Dedicated reservations.
